title: Apogee Financial - Private VPC Discovery
summary: Intro discovery focused on Private/VPC deployment for regulated financial workloads. Discussed VPC peering vs PrivateLink/endpoint models, IP allowlisting, region constraints, KMS/HSM integration, SSO and audit logs. Agreed next steps: share network diagram, security pack, draft architecture for VPC endpoints and pilot proposal.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for latency and cost
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate it. uh quick roll call?
[00:10] Lena (Apogee): Lena here.
[00:12] Mark (Apogee): Mark here.
[00:13] Daniel (Apogee): Daniel -- hi.
[00:15] Ben (Redwood SE): Ben on my side.
[00:18] Maya: Cool, so the plan today is to understand your networking constraints and security bar for a Private/VPC deployment of Redwood. we'll cover peering, private endpoints, region limits, and answer any compliance questions. does that work?
[00:30] Lena: Yep, perfect. high level we are evaluating where to run inference for a few internal apps — credit decisioning, fraud detection. data is sensitive so we need private connectivity and KMS integration. Timeline: POC in next 6-8 weeks. budget TBD.
[00:45] Maya: Got it. can you walk me through your infra? where do you run most workloads, cloud, regions, clusters?
[00:52] Daniel: we are on aws, prod in us-east-1 and us-west-2. some DR in eu-west-1 for Euro customers. VPCs per account, central security account with Transit Gateway.
[01:05] Mark: security requirements — no internet egress from workloads that process PII, we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, KMS with customer-managed keys, and SOC2 is a must.
[01:18] Ben: great, that's super common. quick question: are you leaning toward VPC peering (classic) or PrivateLink-style private endpoints?
[01:26] Lena: we actually don't have a strong preference yet; what's Redwood's recommendation?
[01:30] Ben: for low-latency inference inside your VPC, we usually recommend PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink) endpoints — that keeps traffic within AWS backbone and avoids cross-account peering complexity. Peering is simpler sometimes but doesn't support AWS-managed endpoints the same way and can get messy with Transit Gateway routing.
[01:48] Maya: to add, with Private deployment we can offer two models: 1) Private control plane with customer-managed networking and PrivateLink endpoints to the inference nodes, or 2) Dedicated deployment where Redwood manages reserved capacity in a VPC we connect to via peering or Transit Gateway. Each has tradeoffs on setup complexity and egress control.
[02:10] Mark: Can you expand on egress? if we use PrivateLink, does anything still go out to the public internet?
[02:17] Ben: In a proper PrivateLink flow, API calls from your services to Redwood endpoints stay in AWS network. However, you need to ensure your NAT/EIP rules don't silently route something out — for example, if kernels or telemetry are configured to reach out. Redwood's default hosted offering talks out to telemetry endpoints, but in Private we can disable outbound telemetry or route it to your collectors.
[02:40] Daniel: latency is important for us — sub 200ms tail for small requests. can you get us numbers for models and quantization choices?
[02:48] Maya: yes, Ben will capture expected P99 numbers for the model family you care about. for the pilot we'll recommend a small model variant to hit latency SLOs and then optimize.
[02:58] Ben: note — sometimes the transcript will call KV cache "K V cash" in docs, haha. for latency, running inference in same AZ is ideal. with PrivateLink you can get AZ-local endpoints but if we're cross-AZ there is a small hop.
[03:12] Lena: region constraints: we need data residency for EU customers (eu-west-1). can Redwood deploy private nodes in eu-west-1?
[03:20] Maya: yes, we support private deployments in multiple regions. provisioning timeline varies: usually 2-4 weeks to stand up a private environment in a new region depending on capacity.
[03:31] Mark: KMS / HSM — we require CMKs in our account and HSM backed keys for encryption at rest. how does Redwood integrate?
[03:40] Ben: we can integrate with your KMS for key wrapping. for HSM-backed CMKs we can support envelope encryption where your CMK encrypts a data key and Redwood stores only the encrypted data key; Redwood never has the plain key. We also have audit hooks for key usage. For on-prem HSMs we'll need a secure egress or VPN — that's a slightly more complex path.
[04:05] Daniel: SSO — we use Okta, SAML 2.0. need RBAC.
[04:09] Maya: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; RBAC mapping can be configured to align with your groups. we'll share documentation.
[04:18] Mark: Audit logs — we need forwarding to our SIEM (Splunk). can logs be pushed from the control plane to our logging account?
[04:27] Ben: yes — in Private deployment we can configure log forwarding to your account via Kinesis/Firehose or S3 bucket with bucket policies. We'll provide log schema and sample events.
[04:39] Lena: network IP ranges — we must allowlist IPs. how static are your endpoints?
[04:44] Ben: with PrivateLink you usually create ENIs in your VPC and traffic goes through that, so there aren't the same ephemeral public IPs. For Dedicated hosted endpoints that live in Redwood's managed VPCs, we publish a set of egress ranges you can allowlist but they can change with scaling. For strict allowlist needs, PrivateLink or an in-VPC deployment is better.
[05:05] Maya: also if you do VPC peering via Transit Gateway there are route tables to manage. some customers prefer dedicated because then we can guarantee CIDR ranges and advertise them in a peering connection.
[05:18] Mark: what about TLS termination? do you do TLS at the edge or inside the VPC?
[05:24] Ben: we terminate TLS on the PrivateLink endpoint in your VPC, or we can proxy TLS to the instance level. all data in transit is TLS, and for mTLS we can negotiate mutual TLS if you need client certs.
[05:36] Daniel: is there any requirement for a NAT gateway?
[05:39] Ben: if your nodes need to pull container images or patches from the internet, you'd need a NAT or an image mirror in your repo. Redwood can provide images to a registry in your account for air-gapped setups.
[05:52] Lena: compliance — can you provide SOC2 reports and pen test summaries?
[05:56] Maya: yes, we'll send our security pack with SOC2 Type II, ISO summary, pen test notes, and our data processing addendum.
[06:05] Mark: cost — if we go Dedicated in our VPC vs using Redwood-hosted PrivateLink, how does pricing differ?
[06:12] Maya: Dedicated reserved capacity has a fixed monthly commitment for GPUs (lower per-token cost) but higher upfront. Hosted PrivateLink has lower initial commitment but higher usage rates. we'll put both options in the pilot proposal with estimated TCO for your workload.
[06:27] Daniel: for the POC we want a small footprint: 2 GPUs, logging + audit hook, KMS integration, and perf benchmarks against our latency targets.
[06:36] Maya: reasonable. for success criteria can you confirm: 1) P99 latency under 200ms for short prompts, 2) integration with your KMS, 3) audit logs flowing to your SIEM, and 4) no egress to public internet for PII flows?
[06:50] Lena: yes that's right.
[06:52] Ben: technical note — when you test, please give us representative prompt distributions and payload sizes; batching behavior changes with request size and affects latency/cost.
[07:03] Daniel: we'll prepare a sample workload — mostly short prompts (20-80 tokens), and some bulk embedding jobs overnight.
[07:11] Mark: how does model versioning and rollouts work in private? we need controlled rollouts and canary tests.
[07:18] Ben: rollouts are supported; we expose per-route model pins and can do traffic-split for canary. monitoring integrates with your observability stacks.
[07:27] Maya: any concerns on your side we haven't covered?
[07:30] Mark: one more — do you support cross-account VPC peering via TGW with our security account as the hub?
[07:35] Ben: yes, Transit Gateway peering model works. we'll share a networking diagram and recommended route tables.
[07:43] Lena: perfect.
[07:45] Maya: i'll summarize next steps at the end, but Ben will capture action items.
[07:50] Ben: cool.
[20:00] Maya: jumping ahead a bit — typical pitfalls: not mirroring images in air-gapped, forgetting to open egress for KMS endpoints, and underestimating AZ locality for latency.
[20:15] Daniel: good to know.
[27:30] Mark: what's the expected lead time to spin up a pilot in us-east-1 using PrivateLink?
[27:36] Ben: we can usually stand up endpoints and small fleet in 1-2 weeks if there is no unusual security gating; if you need a new region or HSM integration it extends to 3-4 weeks.
[27:48] Lena: ok. for the SIEM forwarding, we need sample events.
[27:52] Ben: we'll attach a sample log pack.
[30:04] Maya: i'll also note that our Dedicated option can be colocated into your account in some cases — it's a managed private instance inside your VPC, depends on contract.
[30:16] Daniel: any quotas or limits we should be aware of?
[30:19] Ben: there's a default token per-second concurrency cap but for Dedicated we set throughput targets. We'll work with your SRE to size.
[35:00] Mark: what about data retention and delete policies?
[35:04] Maya: in Private deployments, logs and data retention policies can be configured; we can commit to retention windows and deletion upon request. For hosted, we have default retention and can negotiate for enterprise.
[40:00] Lena: ok, sounds good. next steps?
[40:05] Maya: yes — here's what we'll do.
[40:08] Ben: action items incoming.
[40:10] Maya: First, Ben will draft a network diagram and pilot architecture for PrivateLink in us-east-1 with KMS integration and log forwarding. Second, we'll send the security pack and SOC2. Third, we'll propose pricing for both Dedicated reserved and PrivateLink-hosted pilot. and fourth, schedule a deep-dive with your networking/infra team next week.
[40:30] Lena: works for us.
[40:32] Daniel: can we get the proposed deep-dive time in the morning PST?
[40:36] Maya: yes, we'll send options.
[41:00] Mark: thanks all.
[41:04] Maya: thanks for the time. I'll close with the recap in the notes.
[52:00] (call ended)
